land.text: Bali, from the Gelgel kingdom that 'began to break up' after 1651

predecessors.note: Cliopatria's Balinese Kingdom row ends 1686 and Bali starts 1687; the Balinese Kingdom (Gelgel) dossier ends in 1686 with the same Nine Kingdoms period 1686-1908.

land.text: all of Bali under 'the total rule of the Dutch over Bali' after the 1908 assault on Klungkung

successors.note: Buleleng and Jembrana had gone in 1849, Karangasem in 1894 and Badung in 1906.

capitals.name: Klungkung (Semarapura)
capitals.note: 'In 1686 a new royal seat was established in Klungkung', four km north of Gelgel; its rulers (title Dewa Agung) could not maintain power over all of Bali, which the page says was split into nine minor kingdoms. Klungkung is the nominal paramount seat; each of the nine had its own court. Coordinates are approximate (the page gives none).

keyframe_review.note: 7,719 km2 for 1687-1848 against the Bali infobox 5,582.83 km2 (ratio 1.38, within the factor of two; the gridded shape is about 6.3 k km2). The shape is the whole island, which the Nine Kingdoms covered between them. Neither page opened gives the borders between the kingdoms or dates for when each arose, so the island is one shape and the internal borders are not drawn.

correction.text: shape unchanged (the island without Buleleng and Jembrana) but it holds only for 1849-1893; from 1894 Karangasem is also gone, see the new keyframe bali_1894

keyframe_review.note: 3,773 km2: the island without the north coast and Jembrana, which matches the page's 1849 entry: Bangli helped the Dutch attack Buleleng, which allowed the Dutch to take control of Buleleng and Jembrana. Cliopatria keeps Karangasem inside this shape to 1907, but the page says that in 1894 the Dutch defeated the Balinese ruler of Lombok, and Lombok and Karangasem were added to their possessions. The verdict changes only the years.

correction.text: the 1849 shape without Karangasem, added to the Dutch possessions in 1894 together with Lombok (a 25 km radius around Amlapura is the researcher's reading of Karangasem)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's 1849 shape runs to 1904 with Karangasem inside; the page dates the Dutch acquisition of Karangasem to 1894. The extent of Karangasem is not on the page.

correction.text: holds for 1906-1908: the 1849 shape without Karangasem (1894) and without Badung, whose royal house was eliminated by the Dutch assaults at Sanur in 1906; 1905 itself is covered by bali_1894

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria draws 1905-1907 unchanged; the History of Bali page has the Badung royal house eliminated in 1906 and the Klungkung assault of 1908 establishing 'the total rule of the Dutch over Bali', so the state ends in 1908, one year after Cliopatria's last year. Tabanan, Gianyar and Bangli are not dated on the pages, so they are left in until 1908.

region.text: Bali, split into nine minor kingdoms with the paramount seat at Klungkung

ledger.note: 1686-1687: the Gelgel kingdom gives way to the Nine Kingdoms of Bali. 'After 1651 the Gelgel kingdom began to break up due to internal conflicts'; 'In 1686 a new royal seat was established in Klungkung'; the island was split into nine minor kingdoms (Klungkung, Buleleng, Karangasem, Mengwi, Badung, Tabanan, Gianyar, Bangli and Jembrana, per the page). The page dates the seat to 1686 and gives no founding dates for the nine; Cliopatria starts the row in 1687 (the Gelgel dossier ends in 1686).

region.text: Buleleng and Jembrana, the north coast where 'Dutch political and economic control over Bali began in the 1840s'

ledger.note: 1846: the first Dutch military expedition against north Bali. 'A series of three military expeditions occurred between 1846 and 1849.' Jelantik initially countered the first two (page wording), so the ground was held, not taken, until 1849; the month and the landing place are not on the page.
1849: the third expedition ends the contest for the north coast, the king of Buleleng and his retinue dying in a puputan (the page places it in the same passage but gives no date).

1849: the Dutch take Buleleng and Jembrana. The page: Bangli helped the Dutch attack Buleleng, which allowed the Dutch to take control of Buleleng and Jembrana. The first Dutch resident controller reached Singaraja on 12 August 1855.

region.text: Karangasem, 'added to their possessions' by the Dutch with Lombok

ledger.note: 1894: the Dutch take Karangasem. The page (1894): the Dutch defeated the Balinese ruler of Lombok, and Lombok and Karangasem were added to their possessions. Cliopatria keeps Karangasem inside its Bali shape until 1907; the radius is the researcher's reading.

1906: the Dutch destroy the Badung royal house. The page: Dutch assaults at Sanur in 1906 led to the elimination of the Badung royal house and about 1,000 deaths. The Bali page: the royal family and followers chose ritual suicide (puputan) rather than surrender. The extent of Badung is the researcher's reading.

region.text: the rest of Bali under Klungkung's Dewa Agung and the remaining kingdoms

ledger.note: 1908: the Dutch assault on Klungkung ends Balinese rule. The page (1908): a similar massacre occurred during a Dutch assault on Klungkung, which ended the Majapahit dynasty's rule and established 'the total rule of the Dutch over Bali'. The Bali page confirms 'a similar mass suicide occurred in the face of a Dutch assault in Klungkung'.
1908: the Nine Kingdoms end with the fall of Klungkung and Bali becomes Dutch; Cliopatria ends the row in 1907.

wars.name: Dutch expeditions against Buleleng
wars.outcome: The Dutch, helped by Bangli in 1849, defeat Buleleng and take Buleleng and Jembrana; the king of Buleleng and his retinue die in a puputan.
wars.note: 'A series of three military expeditions occurred between 1846 and 1849.' The page does not date 1848 separately. The Bali page: Dutch control began in the 1840s on the north coast.

wars.name: Balinese expedition to Blambangan (1814)
wars.outcome: The page gives no result; it records only the clash.
wars.note: The page: in 1814 the rajas of Buleleng and Karangasem sent an expedition against Blambangan, 'where they fought British Sepoys in February 1814', after Raffles abolished slavery. The war moved no border in the Bali shape, which does not include Blambangan.

wars.name: Dutch intervention in Lombok and Karangasem (1894)

zones.text: Karangasem, added to the Dutch possessions with Lombok in 1894

wars.outcome: The Dutch defeat the Balinese ruler of Lombok, 'adding both Lombok and Karangasem to their possessions'.
wars.note: Added by the se-02-h reviewer from the History of Bali page's 1894 entry (the Dutch defeated the Balinese ruler of Lombok, adding both Lombok and Karangasem to their possessions); it is the war behind the 1894 loss in the ledger. Lombok lies outside this dossier's shape (see notes: karangasem-lombok). The zone is the same Amlapura radius as the 1894 loss.

wars.name: Dutch intervention in Bali (1906)
wars.outcome: The Dutch eliminate the Badung royal house in a puputan; about 1,000 die.
wars.note: The Bali page: 'The Dutch mounted large naval and ground assaults at the Sanur region in 1906.' The Wikipedia article with this title is linked from the Bali page but was not opened (page budget).

wars.name: Dutch intervention in Bali (1908)
wars.outcome: A mass suicide at Klungkung ends the dynasty and establishes the total rule of the Dutch over Bali.
wars.note: The Wikipedia article with this title is linked from the Bali page but was not opened (page budget). The History of Bali page also names a 'war of the Rajas' of 1884-1894 that gave the Dutch a pretext to intervene.

certainty.note: The island coast is natural, but the borders between the nine kingdoms and the Balinese holdings on Lombok and in Blambangan are not on the pages.
The cuts of 1849 (Buleleng, Jembrana), 1894 (Karangasem) and 1906 (Badung) follow kingdom lands whose borders the pages do not give.

notes: Cliopatria's 'Bali' (1687-1907) is the successor of the Gelgel kingdom (Balinese Kingdom, ended 1686) and draws the Nine Kingdoms of Bali as one polity: Klungkung (Dewa Agung, nominal paramount), Buleleng, Karangasem, Mengwi, Badung, Tabanan, Gianyar, Bangli and Jembrana, which the History of Bali page says fought one another. The pages give no founding dates and no borders for them, so they could not be drawn separately; if the project wants them as tints the nine need dossiers (not Cliopatria rows). Life span: Cliopatria ends 1907, the History of Bali page puts the total Dutch rule in 1908 (Klungkung), so the dossier ends in 1908 and the 1905-1907 shape is adjusted. Balinese holdings outside the Cliopatria shape that the pages touch only at their end: western Lombok under the Balinese ruler of Lombok (Karangasem) until the Dutch defeated him in 1894; the Balinese dossier (Gelgel) has the earlier Lombok rule; the pages opened give no start year, so a Karangasem-Lombok dossier or a gap-filler should open 'Lombok' and 'Karangasem'. 1814: the rajas of Buleleng and Karangasem sent an expedition against Blambangan and fought British Sepoys in February 1814 (no land change). 1808: a treaty with the king of Badung was signed but not implemented after Java fell to the British in 1811; Raffles visited Bali in 1815. Cliopatria neighbours: Blambangan 1687-1743 and the Dutch Republic/Batavian Republic as 'neighbours' 1744-1802 are the Cliopatria Dutch shapes (Java), nothing on the pages ties Bali to them before the 1840s; the Qajar Dynasty in 1895-1897 is a Cliopatria artifact. Gazetteer: 'Amlapura' (Karangasem) is not in places.jsonl; Denpasar is.
